A polished, real architectural photograph of advertising inside a modern public building: Our wall display is fixed to the back wall of a brushed brass hotel lift car with the doors open.

References: Image 1 is THE WALL DISPLAY: exact shape, thin black bezel, flat wall mount. No logo. The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera in the open doorway at screen height, 35mm lens, f/5.6, square to the back wall. The screen fills about 50 percent of the frame width on the centre line, sharp; the brass walls and a slim handrail frame it; soft warm downlight from the ceiling. Nobody is in frame.

Place: The calm, spotless interior of a modern public building as each shot names it: polished terrazzo or stone floors, tall glass walls, brushed steel and pale stone; nothing else unless the shot names it.

Light: Clean soft daylight through large glass walls mixed with even architectural ceiling light; the polished floor carries soft true reflections that fade out gently; the design surface is the brightest surface.

Palette and grade: Clean neutral architecture: warm pale stone, soft greys, brushed steel, true whites, a little soft sky blue through the glass; the design surface pure neutral white. The same grade on every image of the collection.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph in a real public building, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, never a small sign in a wide hall. It is an unstaged photograph of a real place in use, polished and spotless. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. The design surface is bright and clean without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. Floor reflections blend away softly, never ending in a hard line. Every screen and lightbox is a real commercial unit with real thickness, a slim frame and real fixings, lit like a real panel, never a flat glowing shape pasted on the wall.

Design surface: THE WALL DISPLAY SHOWS A PLAIN WHITE FULL-SCREEN IMAGE, glowing bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, evenly lit edge to edge yet not blown out, with crisp corners meeting its thin dark frame; nothing crosses it.

Finish: Shot like premium architectural photography on a medium-format camera with a shift lens: straight verticals, crisp detail, natural colour, a gentle film softness in the highlights; real, never a render.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, any image or text on the design surface, any object not named in the shot, tiny far-away people, haze, bloom or glow, a clean smooth 3D render look.
